children: Swiss annual inflation jumped to its highest level in nearly three years in October, government data showed on Tuesday, as a big increase in petrol prices pushed overall prices higher.
- The 1.5% increase in prices was the highest annual rise since December 2023, and comes as the Iran war kept crude and refined-fuel supplies tight, raising prices at the pumps.
- Marking an acceleration from the 1.0% rate in September, the figure also exceeded economist forecasts for a 1.3% rise in a Reuters poll.
- Fuel costs were the biggest driver for the increase, with petrol prices 40% more expensive compared with October 2025.
- Core inflation, which removed the effect of energy, fuel, as well as fresh and seasonal products was 0.5% higher in October 2026 year on year.
- Month on month, Swiss inflation was up 0.2%, higher than the 0% rate in September.
- The Swiss National Bank, which targets an inflation rate of 0-2%, declined to comment on the figures.
- The central bank, which has kept its main interest rates at 0%, is due to give its next interest rate decision on December 10.
